tests.what: Checks that every timestamp is a real date inside a plausible window, neither before the earliest possible record nor in the future, and that records arrive at the expected interval.
thresholds: before 1990 or in the future
gap longer than the expected interval

tests.what: Checks that latitude and longitude are valid coordinates on Earth.
thresholds: latitude outside ±90 or longitude outside ±180

tests.what: Works out the speed implied by consecutive positions and flags jumps faster than the vessel or gear can move, which point to GPS errors.
thresholds: mobile gear, 8 to 30 knots
over 30 knots
tests.discussion: Confirm the limits: based on GPS accuracy or on fishing speed, and whether they vary by gear.

tests.what: Checks that each value lies within what the sensor can measure or, when the sensor is unknown, within the limits found anywhere in the ocean.
thresholds: outside the sensor's range from the manufacturer table
sensor unknown: outside −2.5 to 40 °C, 0 to 11000 dbar, 2 to 42 PSU
tests.discussion: Sensor tables incomplete. Decide whether two inner tiers, calibrated range and operating range, give 2 and 3.

tests.what: Flags a single value that differs sharply from both the value before it and the value after it.
thresholds: difference to both neighbours over 6 °C above 200 m, 2 °C below, or 0.9 PSU
tests.discussion: Absolute differences or standard deviations. No pressure threshold yet.

tests.what: Flags a run of identical readings, the sign of a sensor that has stopped responding.
thresholds: 3 to 5 identical values within 0.001
more than 5
tests.discussion: Counts and tolerance for "identical" (0.001 or 0.01 °C). Row counts mislead on fixed gear, where sampling slows at rest; count time instead.

tests.what: Checks that the sensor was calibrated within the manufacturer's recommended interval before the measurement was taken.
thresholds: past the manufacturer's recalibration interval
no calibration date
no timestamp
tests.discussion: We need all manufacturers' information to apply this flag.

tests.what: Compares each value with what is normal for that place and season and flags values far outside it.
thresholds: outside the seasonal mean ± N standard deviations, WOA or regional
tests.discussion: Climatology source and coastal accuracy; our data are meant to improve the climatologies.

tests.what: Detects a sensor fouled by sediment after the gear touches the seabed, seen as distorted readings as the gear comes back up.
thresholds: fouling signature on the ascent
tests.discussion: Detection criteria per parameter still to write.

tests.what: Compares the first and last samples of the bottom segment of a tow and flags the whole tow when they differ too much; two points cannot tell sensor drift from a real change in the water.
thresholds: bottom segment under 24 h, first and last temperature more than 3 °C apart: whole tow
bottom segment under 24 h, first and last salinity more than 8 PSU apart: whole tow
bottom segment of 24 h or more: not checked
tests.discussion: Not a drift test: trawls cross fronts and bottom temperature changes with the tide. Soaks of 24 h or more, where drift would show, are never checked. One spike at either end is enough to trigger it. Good descent and ascent samples get 3 too. Same limits in every region and depth. Long-term calibration drift belongs to delayed mode.

tests.what: Flags positions that fall on land according to a land mask such as ETOPO5.
thresholds: on land per ETOPO5 or better
tests.discussion: Kept off because land masks are poor near shore. If a program enables it, 3 rather than 4.

tests.what: Checks that the positions fit how the gear works: fixed gear should stay close to where it was deployed.
thresholds: fixed gear, deployment to retrieval over 200 m
mobile gear: to be defined; drifting gear: not applied
tests.discussion: We need to differentiate mobile from fixed gear. This should not apply to drifting gear.

tests.what: Flags a value that changes from the previous one by much more than the normal variability of its segment.
thresholds: change from the previous value over 3 standard deviations of the segment

tests.what: Flags the first readings after the gear enters the water in extreme cold, when the sensor, chilled in the air before deployment, takes a few seconds to adjust to the real water temperature.
thresholds: not defined
tests.discussion: Separate test, or surface thresholds inside the spike test.

tests.what: Flags samples on the descent and ascent where the gear moves up or down faster than the thermistor can follow; despite its name it measures vertical speed, not the sensor's response time.
thresholds: descent or ascent, vertical speed 1 to 2 dbar/s
descent or ascent, vertical speed over 2 dbar/s
fishing segment: not applied
tests.discussion: Rename it, since it measures vertical speed. One limit for every sensor: use each sensor's response time, its sampling rate and the temperature gradient instead. Flag 4 removes the data from GTS and ERDDAP. Meant for the top 10 dbar but applied at every depth. Repeated timestamps give an infinite speed and a 4. The lagged samples after a fast stretch are not flagged.

tests.what: Checks the deepest value of a profile, where the gear turns from descent to ascent, and flags it when it jumps away from its neighbour.
thresholds: proposal: bottom value more than 1 °C from its neighbour
tests.discussion: Threshold, what counts as adjacent, profiling gear only, whether salinity gets the same.
